newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian groups assail Italy on peace proposal.
newsitem.headline: Algerian groups assail Italy on peace proposal.

text.p: Algeria's three main radical secularist groups blasted Italy over a proposed peace initiative to halt bloodshed in Algeria and hailed the United States for keeping out of similar diplomatic moves.

"What the United States rejected with lucidity and wisdom was taken over by another state, Italy," said the Rally for Democracy and Culture (RCD), Algerian Movement for Justice and Development (MAJD) and former communist Ettahadi party in a joint statement distributed on Thursday.

The opposition groups were reacting to Italian foreign ministry undersecretary Piero Fassino who said this week that the West had underestimated the seriousness of Algeria's civil strife and called on the European Union to lead an initiative to halt bloodshed.
Fassino said Italy planned to present a peace proposal at a meeting of foreign ministers of Italy, Spain and France on February 3.
The three Algerian groups said such an idea showed an "unremitting effort to force Algeria to abdicate (responsibility) in the face of Moslem fundamentalism".
The joint statement said the Italian move was unbelievable, knowing "that Italy had integrated the Red Brigades into its legal political system."
The Algerian government and its political backers have consistently rejected outside involvement in a bid to end the five-year-old violence.
The three parties also faulted the Algerian foreign ministry saying "once again, the Algerian diplomacy took refuge in silence".

Algeria has not publicly commented on the Italian move but says the North African country's violence can only be solved inside Algeria through dialogue and only between Algerians who reject violence as means to gain power.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which the now outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken a commanding lead.
